questions.question: Explain what is meant by the basic economic problem of scarcity.
questions.expected_answer: Human wants are unlimited, but the resources available to satisfy them (natural, human, capital resources, money and time) are limited. Because wants are greater than resources, people, businesses and government cannot have everything and must make choices.

questions.question: Name the four factors of production (types of resources) and give an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Natural resources, e.g. land, water, minerals; human resources/labour, e.g. a teacher's skills; capital, e.g. machines, buildings, tools; entrepreneurship, e.g. a person starting a bakery by combining the other resources.

questions.question: Define opportunity cost and identify it: Zanele has R80 and must choose between a book (her second choice) and a concert ticket (her first choice).
questions.expected_answer: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative given up when making a choice. Zanele chooses the concert ticket, so the opportunity cost is the book.
